answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Reaching the oasis of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Each submission hangs on the ivory of a task receipt, and the bridge is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The design leans on reciprocity-weighted attestation, split across independent auditors, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short.
